article_title: Research on the student-centered research feedback experimental teaching model to enhance the effectiveness of pharmacology experimental teaching.
citation: Miao C, Chen J, Li Y, Xia A, Song Y, Xu C, Mao Y, Wang X. (2026). Research on the student-centered research feedback experimental teaching model to enhance the effectiveness of pharmacology experimental teaching. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000051199
title: Quantitative evaluation of learning process (QELP) instrument for pharmacology experimental courses
description: QELP is a multi-component evaluation developed by the college's Experimental (Training) Teaching Center, "divided into 4 aspects: online scores, midterm scores, experimental report scores, final scores, and composite scores (the average score of the above 4 items)." Each evaluation is scored to a maximum of 100 points, with final scores covering 10 teaching projects averaged across key experimental-operation scoring points rated by the guiding teacher during class. The article uses QELP to compare TPETM and RFPETM groups across the learning process.
requirements: Key experimental operations defined as scoring points for each teaching project
constraints: Developed by a single institution's teaching center; final-score distribution used five fixed evaluation levels
key_sources: Miao C, Chen J, Li Y, Xia A, Song Y, Xu C, Mao Y, Wang X. (2026). Research on the student-centered research feedback experimental teaching model to enhance the effectiveness of pharmacology experimental teaching. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000051199

article_title: Particle Physics in High School Part I: Quantum Electrodynamics
citation: Gláuber Carvalho Dorsch, Thaisa Carneiro da Cunha Guio. (2021). Particle Physics in High School Part I: Quantum Electrodynamics. https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.04946
title: A high-school teaching sequence introducing Particle Physics through Quantum Electrodynamics
description: The article introduces a multi-part teaching sequence that brings Particle Physics into the high-school curriculum with emphasis on scientific literacy. It starts from atomic structure and the discovery of the electron, moves through the electromagnetic interaction, electromagnetic waves, wave-particle duality and photons, and culminates in the QED description in which "a interação entre cargas elétricas é mediada pela troca de fótons". The sequence is designed to intersect with content usually taught in high school, so Particle Physics can be included without sacrificing classical physics learning.
requirements: A teacher willing to adapt the reference material to their own classroom purposes rather than follow it as a fixed recipe
constraints: Sections 2.7 and 2.8 on QED may be less familiar to high-school teachers, so the text also serves teacher training in that theoretical paradigm
target_learning_goals: Understanding key concepts of particle physics and quantum electrodynamics
examples: The sequence was applied in an elective context at a full-time public school in Espírito Santo, Brazil
key_sources: Gláuber Carvalho Dorsch, Thaisa Carneiro da Cunha Guio. (2021). Particle Physics in High School Part I: Quantum Electrodynamics. https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.04946

article_title: Building a Quantum Engineering Undergraduate Program
citation: Asfaw, A., Blais, A., Brown, K. R., et al. (2021). Building a Quantum Engineering Undergraduate Program. https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01311
title: Quantum engineering minor plus quantum track within engineering majors as the program structure for quantum-proficient engineers
description: The article proposes that a complete undergraduate quantum engineering program be built as a minor "accessible to all STEM majors" and a "quantum track directly integrated into individual engineering majors", and that "such programs typically require only three or four newly developed courses" complementing existing classes. This keeps students' broader engineering degree intact while adding quantum specialization, fitting the article's T-shaped engineer goal.
requirements: Requires only three or four newly developed courses complementing existing engineering and science classes on most larger campuses
constraints: The article calls a future standalone quantum engineering major premature at this stage
target_learners: STEM majors at four-year colleges and research universities
target_learning_goals: quantum proficiency at the bachelor's level
breadth across quantum technologies and specializations
examples: The article notes three existing working examples of the minor and one current working example of the quantum track within an engineering major
key_sources: Asfaw, A., Blais, A., Brown, K. R., et al. (2021). Building a Quantum Engineering Undergraduate Program. https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01311
